analysis: The method `drawArrowsForTargets` is designed to draw arrows for targets in a game interface, using the `getLocationOnScreen` method to get the location of components on the screen. The `getLocationOnScreen` method can throw an `IllegalComponentStateException` if the component is not showing on the screen. In the provided code, the `getLocationOnScreen` method is called multiple times, each time on a different object (e.g., `data`, `p`, `permanent.getCardLocationOnScreen()`). However, there is no explicit check or validation to ensure that these components are showing on the screen before calling `getLocationOnScreen`. Therefore, the `IllegalComponentStateException` is not avoided in the current implementation.
remark: The `IllegalComponentStateException` will be thrown if any of the components (e.g., `data`, `p`, or `permanent.getCardLocationOnScreen()`) are not showing on the screen when `getLocationOnScreen` is called. Since there is no check to ensure the components are showing, this exception can occur if the component is not visible or has not been added to a visible container.
